rationale: Zulip's first-party docs give an installer for running a self-hosted server and state that self-hosters get the same software as Zulip Cloud. Export/import tools allow moving between Cloud and your own servers, and community users confirm running their own instances on fully open-source code. Community reports of install friction (Debian/Ubuntu-only, a dedicated server or VM, 4GB RAM recommended) limit the experience but do not contradict the capability. Missing for 10: evidence of broad OS support and a well-working container deployment.

rationale: Zulip's docs show public, web-public and private channel types. Subscription is role-gated: everyone except guests can subscribe to any public channel, and private channel messages are a distinct class. However, the evidence does not document admin-side membership controls such as adding or removing members, restricting who can join, or managing private channel access. Missing for 10: documented admin membership management for channels, how private channel access is granted and controlled, channel creation and permission settings, independent hands-on corroboration.

rationale: Zulip's own documented topic model gives each side conversation in a channel its own topic. Community users credit this threading model and say threads can be created 'on the fly from existing messages', but the docs never describe replying to a specific message so the thread stays attached to it. Usability complaints (e.g. posting to an unexpected thread) are UX caveats, not a contradiction of the capability. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of replying from a specific message into a thread anchored to that original message, and documentation of the reply/thread UI flow.
